thread:
maria: seeing intermittent ~0.3-1% packet loss for east-west pod traffic between gpu-pool nodes in us-east-2 during nightly backfills starting ~03:20 UTC. Affects gke-gpu-backfill pods only. anyone else?
raj: yup saw alerts + increased GRPC timeouts on a few jobs. started around the same time.
nicole: do we have mtus mismatched on the host vs geneve device? backfills push larger payloads which can trigger GSO/GRO bugs.
tim: quick capture from one affected node (trimmed):
```
09:38:15.123456 IP 10.42.3.12 > 10.42.7.45: UDP, length 1360
09:38:15.123457 IP 10.42.7.45 > 10.42.3.12: UDP, length 68
... dropped payloads where outer len < inner expected, suspicious GENEVE drop
```
infra-bot: [alert] kernel dmesg shows repeated "geneve: bad checksum" on node ip-10-0-52-7.us-east-2 (3 occurrences)
maria: ran `ip link show` on the node, geneve0 mtu=1450, docker0 1500, underlying nic mtu=9000 (we use jumbo).
nicole: aha — underlying NIC is 9000, geneve is 1450, docker 1500. Could be fragmenting + GSO edge-case. also check offloads: `ethtool -k eth0`
tim: ethtool dump: `tx-checksum-ip-generic: on`, `generic-segmentation-offload: on`, `generic-receive-offload: on`
raj: these offloads interacting with encap can cause inner packet get mis-assembled when host MTU < inner expected. Backfills might be sending larger batched requests so more segments.
oncall-sre: can we repro by forcing large payloads between two pods on same node vs cross-node? if same node->less likely network, cross-node->network stack.
maria: repro script: `dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=2 | nc -l 8000` on receiver and curl from sender with --data-binary, I see ~0.5% failures cross-node, none same-node.
nicole: suggests temporary mitigation: disable GSO/GRO on overlay interfaces on a small canary set: `ethtool -K geneve0 gso off gro off` and monitor. low risk and quick to rollback.
raj: good plan. propose canary on 3 nodes in us-east-2-gpu-pool during next maintenance window. also file INFRA-4729 to track.
oncall-sre: i'm +1 but want to capture pcap before change for vendor if needed.
maria: captured 30MB pcap, uploaded to S3 at s3://rwinf-observability/geneve-backfill/2145006789/pcap.zip
tim: after disabling GSO on one canary node overnight, observed drop rate down to ~0.02% and gRPC timeouts returned to baseline.
nicole: long-term fixes: consider setting consistent MTU across host/overlay endpoints, or enable small fragment coalescing in tun driver. also check kernel versions for known geneve GSO bugs (recent kernel 6.x fix).
raj: opened INFRA-4729 with notes + pcap + kernel dmesg + canary results. tagging @neteng for follow-up with vendor and deciding whether to push cluster-wide rollback.
maria: action items: 1) run GSO disable on remaining 2 canaries (now) 2) schedule maintenance to align MTU on host vs overlay 3) vendor escalation if kernel patch needed.
oncall-sre: logging runbook steps into incident doc and will watch CPU/io to ensure no perf regression from disabling offloads. :eyes:
maria: thanks all, keeping this thread for the backfill window. will post a follow-up with cluster-wide decision. :thumbsup:
